sentences.text: 2.  The appellant has been convicted for the offence under Sections 376(2)(I) of IPC, in connection with Children Case No.19 of 2022.
He has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for life years and a fine of Rs.20,000/- for the offence under Section 376(2)(I) of IPC.

3. Heard, the learned counsel for the appellant and learned A.P.P. for the State and have gone through the impugned judgment, the evidence and the Trial Court Records.
4.
Opportunity was given to the State to oppose the bail, which the State availed and opposed.
5. There is delay of six months in lodging the FIR.
Further from the evidence, it is prima facie established that as the marriage was not solemnized between the parties, this criminal proceeding was initiated.
6. Considering the aforesaid fact, we are inclined to allow this Interlocutory application.

Accordingly, upon suspending the sentence, the appellant, namely, Ritik Kumar is directed to be released on bail during the pendency of this appeal, on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.10,000/- (Rs.
Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Session Judge-1-cum Special Judge, Children Court Dhanbad, in connection with Children Case No.19 of 2022 with a condition that the appellant shall appear and mark his attendance before the Registrar, Civil Court, Dhanbad, once in every four months till the disposal of Ritik Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73094377/
1 this appeal.
7. I.A. No.6644 of 2024 stands allowed.
